watchlist.thesis: Procter & Gamble is the strongest fresh large-cap technical setup in the StockLens screen, with an 88 technical score and strong risk/macro posture despite weak news sentiment.
Visa combines an 86 technical score, 88 risk score and solid composite reading, making it a clean liquid momentum candidate ahead of its October 27 earnings event.
Palantir retains a solid 71 composite with 87 fundamental and 79 technical scores, although its macro score remains strongly bearish.
CrowdStrike has an 87 technical score and sector-leading relative strength, but its weak macro and risk scores favor controlled pullbacks over chasing.
Palo Alto Networks remains technically bullish and highly liquid, but its low fundamental and risk scores make the setup more selective than CRWD.
Fortinet remains a liquid cybersecurity momentum candidate, with the October 28 post-market earnings event the dominant near-term catalyst.
Microsoft remains a core cloud and AI leader, but its October 28 earnings event makes any pre-report swing materially gap-sensitive.
Apple offers exceptional liquidity and durable mega-cap trend characteristics, but its November 2 earnings event argues for event-aware sizing.
Salesforce remains a liquid software candidate for orderly pullbacks while investors discriminate between durable software growth and capital-intensive AI trades.
ServiceNow remains a high-liquidity cloud-software trend candidate, but its October 28 earnings event and broader software volatility favor post-event confirmation.
Cloudflare remains a high-beta software momentum name with strong liquidity, best approached after volatility contracts rather than after sharp upside bursts.
Datadog remains a liquid observability leader suitable for momentum continuation if software breadth stabilizes after the current AI-spending shock.
Veeva provides liquid healthcare-software diversification and a cleaner business-model exposure while broader technology leadership remains uneven.
Texas Instruments has a 79 technical score, 81 fundamental score and 86 risk score, making it one of the cleaner semiconductor setups despite a bearish macro backdrop.
Exxon has an 86 technical score and strong risk posture, keeping it among the leading liquid energy momentum names ahead of October 30 results.
Chevron has an 86 technical score and 87 risk score, providing strong energy momentum exposure despite a strongly bearish macro score.
ConocoPhillips remains a liquid upstream energy candidate aligned with current sector leadership, with crude reversals the principal momentum risk.
EOG offers liquid exploration-and-production exposure to the current energy leadership regime while remaining sensitive to oil-price reversals.
Occidental provides higher-beta liquid energy exposure suitable for swings, but commodity and geopolitical volatility require disciplined sizing.
Cheniere provides liquid LNG exposure aligned with energy strength, while its October 29 earnings event makes post-report confirmation preferable.
Marathon Petroleum is a liquid refining momentum candidate benefiting from energy breadth while remaining sensitive to crack spreads and crude volatility.
GE Vernova offers liquid power-infrastructure exposure to the AI electricity-buildout theme, but October 28 earnings and valuation sensitivity argue for confirmation.
Coca-Cola combines a 74 technical score with strong 89 risk and 88 macro scores, offering a defensive trend anchor while high-beta technology remains unstable.

AI-infrastructure financing and return-on-capex concerns remain a broad sector headwind, making confirmed continuation preferable to anticipation.
Alpha Vantage places AMD's earnings on November 3 and the stock remains highly sensitive to AI and semiconductor expectations, so pre-event entry has poor risk/reward.

Applied Materials has an upcoming November 12 earnings event and remains exposed to semiconductor-capex volatility, so wait for post-event confirmation.
KLA reports October 28 and remains coupled to the volatile semiconductor-capex regime, making a pre-event momentum entry unattractive.
Lam Research remains tightly coupled to semiconductor-capex sentiment and was caught in the recent AI-driven sector selloff; wait for sustained relative strength.
